artworks.titleEn: The Virgin of Guadalupe (Virgen de Guadalupe)
artworks.medium: Oil on canvas on wood inlaid with mother-of-pearl
artworks.function: Marian devotion and creole identity
artworks.form: The iconic Virgin stands within radiating mandorla above crescent and angel, framed by apparition scenes
artworks.content: The Guadalupe image is joined to narrative vignettes of Juan Diego’s visions
artworks.context: Enconchado technique and a locally rooted Marian cult articulated New Spanish sacred and cultural identity
recognitionAnchors: Radiant Virgin stands on crescent moon
Mother-of-pearl surface surrounds apparition scenes

artworks.function: Collector display and contemplation of nature and transience
artworks.form: A diagonal mound of fruit, flowers, insects, and reptiles emerges dramatically from darkness
artworks.content: Abundance coexists with bruising, predation, and decay
artworks.context: Ruysch joined scientific observation and virtuoso market painting in the Dutch Republic

artworks.content: A Spanish father, Indigenous mother, and mestizo child embody a named racial category
artworks.context: Casta series naturalized New Spain’s colonial hierarchy while revealing its constructed categories

artworks.titleEn: The Tête à Tête, from Marriage à la Mode
artworks.function: Moral satire and elite art-market display
artworks.form: A stage-like interior packs diagonal glances and symbolic details into a sequential narrative
artworks.content: A disheveled aristocratic couple and exhausted steward expose infidelity, debt, and failed marriage
artworks.context: Hogarth critiqued arranged marriage and elite consumption in a series designed for painted and engraved circulation
recognitionAnchors: Clock reads after noon above bored couple
